B1: Catching Up After Australia

A B1 speaking-first catch-up lesson for talking about a family trip to Australia, with useful phrases, model replies, open questions, and a light Kawara/building comparison.

Start The Catch-Up

A student had just come back from Australia with his wife, his parents, and his aunt. It was a real family trip, not a business trip. He wanted to tell the story in English, but he did not want to sound stiff or unnatural. So he started in a simple way. He...

Continue as You.

Answer the first warm question: “How was Australia?” Give a real answer in 3 to 4 short parts.

Useful phrases

It was a real family trip.

I went with...

The first thing I want to say is...

Starter help

I have just come back from Australia, and...

It was a family trip with...

The trip felt... because...

One model reply

I have just come back from Australia. I went with my wife, my mother, my parents, and my aunt, so it felt like a big family memory, not only sightseeing.

More acceptable replies

Australia was really interesting because I could relax with my family.

It was a little tiring, but I enjoyed talking and walking with everyone.

Tip: Start broad first. Then add who, where, and one feeling.

Tell The Basic Trip Story

After that first line, he told the story in time order. The family stayed in Sydney for three days at the start of the trip. They were tired after the flight, but they were also excited. On the first morning, they woke up early and walked near the harbour....

Continue as You.

Say where you stayed, what you saw first, and why that first day stayed in your memory.

Useful phrases

We stayed in...

It looked bigger than I expected.

Starter help

On the first morning, we...

When I saw the harbour, I...

One model reply

At the start of the trip, we stayed in Sydney. On the first morning, we walked near the harbour, and the Opera House looked bigger than I expected.

More acceptable replies

We were tired after the flight, but we were excited to walk around.

The water and the buildings made the first morning feel special.

Tip: Use past simple for the finished trip: stayed, walked, saw, felt.

Describe Your Family Reactions

That was one of the most memorable moments of the trip. The student’s aunt stopped walking and smiled without saying anything. His father took out his phone at once. His wife quietly said that the building looked like sails on the water. For a few seconds,...

Continue as You.

Choose one person from the trip and describe what they did or said in that moment.

Useful phrases

For a few seconds, we...

Starter help

My wife said that...

My father...

Everyone just...

One model reply

My aunt stopped walking and smiled. My wife said the Opera House looked like sails, and that made the moment easy to remember.

More acceptable replies

My father took photos right away because he wanted to keep the memory.

For a few seconds, we just stood there and looked.

Tip: Small actions make the story feel real.

Talk About The Mood

Later that day, they walked closer and took photos from several angles. They also saw the Harbour Bridge nearby. The area was busy, but it was easy to enjoy. Street sounds mixed with the noise of boats on the water. The family did not rush. They moved slowl...

Continue as You.

Explain whether the trip felt busy, calm, warm, tiring, or shared. Use one reason.

Useful phrases

We did not rush.

That made it feel...

because my parents wanted...

Starter help

We moved slowly because...

That slower pace made...

One model reply

The mood was warm and relaxed. We did not rush because my parents wanted time to rest, so the trip felt more shared.

More acceptable replies

It was busy near the harbour, but our family moved slowly.

I liked the slower pace because we could talk more.

Tip: At B1, add a reason with because or so.

Compare Transport

The family used different kinds of transport during the trip. In Sydney, they walked a lot and also took a train. The student liked the train ride because it was simple and calm. He could look out the window and watch the city change. In another part of the...

Continue as You.

Compare walking, trains, and cars during the trip. Which one created the best memory or the biggest problem?

Useful phrases

The train was calmer than...

The car gave us more freedom, but...

Compared with Japan...

Starter help

Walking was good because...

The car was useful, but...

One model reply

The train was calm because I could look out the window. The car gave us more freedom, but we missed a turn once.

More acceptable replies

Walking helped us see the city slowly.

The car was convenient, but it also made the trip a little stressful.

Tip: Use but to make the answer more natural.

?

Why might travelling by car have caused a small problem during the trip? Use the idea from the text.

You can start like this: Because...

Tell A Small Problem

It was not a serious problem, but it changed the mood for a short time. The student felt nervous because his parents were getting hungry. His aunt laughed and said that every family trip needs one mistake. That joke helped everyone relax. Soon they found a...

Continue as You.

Tell the wrong-turn story or another small travel problem. Make it sound funny or human, not like a failure.

Useful phrases

It was not serious, but...

My aunt joked that...

Later, it became part of the story.

Starter help

At first, I felt...

Later, we laughed because...

One model reply

One small problem was that we drove the wrong way for about twenty minutes. At first, I felt nervous, but my aunt laughed and everyone relaxed.

More acceptable replies

It was annoying at the time, but now it is a funny memory.

We stopped, bought drinks, checked the map, and started again.

Tip: A good catch-up story often includes one small problem and how people reacted.

?

Why did the student feel nervous in this part?

Share Food Details

Food gave the trip many real, happy details. One day, the family ate seafood near the water. They had fish, bread, and fruit. Everything tasted fresh, and the meal felt special because they were together. The student remembered one small surprise. His mothe...

Continue as You.

Talk about one food or drink moment from Australia. Add who liked it and why it was memorable.

Useful phrases

My mother usually does not..., but...

The small surprise was...

Starter help

My mother liked...

The meal felt special because...

One model reply

We ate seafood near the water. My mother usually does not eat much bread at home, but she loved the warm bread and asked for more.

More acceptable replies

I remember the food because it was fresh and everyone looked happy.

Tip: Food is an easy way to make a travel answer longer.

Use Simple Table English

The student also needed simple English for food and drink. At one point, someone asked, “Do we have any water?” The answer was, “Yes, we have some water.” That kind of language fits naturally into a travel story. It is not just grammar from a book. It is th...

Continue as You.

Practise a tiny travel-table exchange with some and any, then add your real detail.

Useful phrases

Could we get some...?

Starter help

Yes, we have some...

We needed... because...

One model reply

Do we have any water? Yes, we have some water. We needed it because the day was hot and we were walking a lot.

More acceptable replies

We had some water in the car, but we needed more.

Tip: Keep this short. It is useful English, not a grammar lecture.

a ” ” a

Continue The Conversation

Explain Weather With Because Or So

The weather in Australia gave them another strong memory. One day was bright and hot. They planned to stay outside longer, but the heat became tiring. So they went indoors for a while and rested. The student could say, “It was hot, so we stayed inside.” He...

Continue as You.

Say what the weather was like and explain one decision with because or so.

Useful phrases

The heat became tiring.

Both sentences sound natural.

Starter help

We stayed inside because...

The weather was..., so...

One model reply

It was hot, so we stayed inside for a while. We stayed inside because the heat became tiring.

More acceptable replies

It was sunny, so we walked in the morning and rested later.

We changed the plan because the weather was hotter than we expected.

Tip: Use so before the result. Use because before the reason.

Continue The Conversation

Talk About A Surprise

The quick change in weather also surprised them. After a warm morning, the sky turned grey and wind moved across the water. The family had not expected that change. The student’s wife had a light jacket in her bag, so she was fine. His aunt did not, so they...

Continue as You.

Describe one unexpected moment, like weather changing or needing to buy something during the trip.

Useful phrases

We had not expected...

We stopped at...

A trip rarely goes exactly as planned.

Starter help

Luckily, my wife...

My aunt needed... so...

One model reply

One unexpected thing was the weather changing quickly. My wife had a light jacket, but my aunt did not, so we stopped and bought one.

More acceptable replies

We did not expect the wind near the water.

It was not a big problem, but it made the day more memorable.

Tip: Unexpected moments are good conversation fuel.

Mention First Nations Culture Respectfully

During the trip, the family also learned a little about First Nations culture in a respectful way. They saw information at a local place they visited and read about the long history of the land. The student understood that these cultures are living cultures...

Continue as You.

Say one careful sentence about learning a little from local information, without pretending to know too much.

Useful phrases

I do not want to say too much, but...

It made me interested to know more.

living cultures

Starter help

I do not know enough to explain deeply, but...

It made me feel...

One model reply

We learned a little about First Nations culture from local information. I do not know enough to explain deeply, but it made me interested to know more.

More acceptable replies

I understood that these are living cultures, not only history.

I would like to learn more carefully before I talk about it in detail.

Tip: Respectful language can be simple and honest.

Bridge To Kawara And Buildings

The student noticed another difference too. Australia felt different from Japan in everyday ways. Some buildings looked lighter and more open. Some houses seemed simpler than houses with traditional tile roofs in Japan. These were not big judgments. They we...

Continue as You.

Compare Australian buildings with Japanese houses or kawara tile roofs. Keep it light and personal.

Useful phrases

It was different from Japan because...

Some roofs looked lighter than...

Traditional tile roofs feel...

Starter help

Australian houses looked...

Compared with Japanese tile roofs...

One model reply

As someone connected to kawara, I noticed that some Australian houses looked lighter and simpler than traditional Japanese tile-roof houses.

More acceptable replies

It made me think about how roofs show culture and climate.

Japanese tile roofs feel heavier and more traditional to me.

Tip: Use the craft connection as a bridge, not as a technical lecture.

Continue The Conversation

Tell The 60-Second Version

By the end, the family trip had a clear shape. They arrived in Australia, stayed in Sydney, saw famous places, used trains and cars, ate fresh food, and managed small surprises. They felt excitement, tiredness, laughter, and a little stress. That mix made t...

Continue as You.

Now tell the whole Australia story in about 60 seconds: who, where, three moments, one comparison, and one feeling.

Useful phrases

One small problem was...

The best memory was...

Compared with Japan...

Starter help

After that, we...

One thing I noticed was...

Overall, I felt...

One model reply

First, I went to Australia with my wife and family. We stayed in Sydney, saw the harbour and the Opera House, ate seafood, and had one small driving mistake. Compared with Japan, some buildings felt lighter and more open. Overall, it was tiring but very warm.

More acceptable replies

The trip was special because I could share it with many family members.

If I tell the story again, I want to describe the people more than only the places.

Tip: Do not list everything. Choose the best 3 moments and connect them smoothly.

Speaking goal

Use this lesson to help the student talk more about Australia: start with a warm catch-up answer, add family memories, explain small surprises, compare Australia with Japan, and finish with a 60-second trip story.
